## trazo

Use when the user asks for an architecture, workflow, ERD or sequence diagram, or an interactive HTML diagram. trazo turns semantic JSON into a laid-out, self-contained HTML file.

1. Pick the type from the request: architecture (components and links), workflow (steps and decisions), erd (tables and foreign keys), sequence (messages between actors).
2. Know the content first. When the diagram describes code, read it first and draw only what you found; never add parts that only sound likely. Keep one level of detail per diagram (services or modules, not both). If the request does not say what to cover and the code does not settle it, ask the user.
3. Run `trazo example <type> > diagram.json` and edit that file. Work in the current directory, not in this skill's folder; in a repository, keep it under docs/diagrams/ so it can be regenerated when the code changes. Run `trazo schema <type>` only when you need a field the example does not show.
4. Never write positions, sizes or colors. Describe the content with `label`, `kind`, `note` and `source`; layout is automatic. Set `source` to the "path/file.ts:line" each part comes from, so the user can verify it.
5. Run `trazo check <file>`. Then run `trazo make <file>`, adding `-o <path>.html` to choose the output, and tell the user the path.
6. If `check` reports errors, each line gives a path and a hint. Fix every listed problem, apply any "did you mean" suggestion, and run `check` again. Edit the file in place; do not rewrite it.
7. Geometry warnings go to stderr and do not fail the run. For `text-overflow` and `label-overlap`, shorten the label. For `edge-through-node` and `node-overlap`, change `direction`, group related nodes or split the diagram. `outside-canvas` and `outside-group` are defects in the tool: do not chase them.
8. Over 60 nodes the tool warns: split into several diagrams.
